The Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Orchestration paper and the Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration paper both propose that multi-agent setups can outperform single Large Language Models (LLMs) [22, 23]. Their orchestration strategies differ in approach. The Multi-Turn Multi-Agent Orchestration paper employs a traditional orchestrator–worker framework, where agents execute sequentially, one at a time [23]. In contrast, the Multi-Agent Collaboration via Evolving Orchestration paper presents a more dynamic approach, where agents interact through evolving orchestration and role-specific prompts [24]. This allows for more flexible and adaptive collaboration among agents. The use of hierarchical evolution of multi-agent RAG and experience-based reflection enables the system to jointly optimize orchestration policy and agent prompts [24]. On the other hand, the traditional orchestrator–worker framework is constrained by sequential execution, limiting coordination and synergies between agents [23]. Overall, both papers contribute to the development of multi-agent systems, but their orchestration strategies reflect different design choices and priorities.
